description: Okra (bhendi, bhindi) is a warm-season vegetable grown almost year-round in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Gujarat and West Bengal. Whitefly-borne yellow vein mosaic and leaf curl viruses are its main threats, so resistant hybrids are preferred.
npk_split: Apply half the N with all P and K at sowing and the remaining N in two equal splits at 30 and 45 days after sowing.

Alternaria leaf spot.name: Alternaria Leaf Spot
Alternaria leaf spot.description: A fungal leaf spot that attacks older and weak leaves in warm, humid weather. Heavy spotting dries the lower leaves and shortens the picking period.
symptoms: Small brown round spots with ring-like (target) markings
Yellow halo around the spots
Spots merge into large dead patches
Older leaves dry and drop
Alternaria leaf spot.spread: Survives on crop debris and spreads by wind and rain splash in warm, humid weather.
Alternaria leaf spot.action: Spray mancozeb 75 WP 2.5 g/L or chlorothalonil 75 WP 2 g/L at the first spots and repeat after 10-15 days.

treatment.name: Mancozeb 75 WP
treatment.notes: Pick marketable pods before spraying and observe the label waiting period.

treatment.name: Chlorothalonil 75 WP
treatment.notes: Alternative protective spray; only where the label lists your crop.

Cercospora leaf spot.name: Cercospora Leaf Spot
Cercospora leaf spot.description: A fungal disease of okra leaves in humid, rainy weather, seen as sooty black mould under the leaf or as brown spots. Severe attack causes leaves to roll, dry and fall.
symptoms: Sooty black mould patches on the underside of the leaf with no clear border
Faint yellow patches on the upper surface above the mould
Brown irregular spots with grey centre and dark margin
Leaves roll, dry and drop
Cercospora leaf spot.spread: Survives on crop residue and spreads by wind and rain splash in humid, rainy weather.
Cercospora leaf spot.action: Spray mancozeb 75 WP 2.5 g/L or carbendazim 50 WP 1 g/L on both leaf surfaces and repeat after 15 days.

treatment.name: Mancozeb 75 WP
treatment.notes: Wet the leaf underside; pick pods before spraying and observe the label waiting period.

Downy mildew.name: Downy Mildew
Downy mildew.cause: Downy-mildew-type oomycete; the species on okra is not well documented
Downy mildew.description: A downy-mildew-type leaf disease that appears in cool, wet weather as yellow patches with downy growth underneath. It is uncommon on okra in India and is easily confused with powdery mildew or Cercospora sooty mould, so check the leaf underside before spraying.
symptoms: Pale yellow, angular patches on the upper leaf surface
Greyish downy growth on the underside below the patches
Patches turn brown and dry
Affected leaves curl and drop early
Downy mildew.spread: Spores spread by wind and rain splash when leaves stay wet for long periods in cool, humid weather.
Downy mildew.action: Remove badly affected leaves, avoid overhead watering, and spray mancozeb 75 WP 2.5 g/L if the patches are spreading in wet weather.

treatment.name: Mancozeb 75 WP
treatment.notes: Protective spray that also covers the common leaf spots if the diagnosis is uncertain; pick pods before spraying and observe the label waiting period.

treatment.name: Wider spacing and drainage
treatment.notes: Keep the crop open and well drained so the leaves dry quickly.

Leaf curl virus.name: Leaf Curl Virus
Leaf curl virus.description: A whitefly-borne virus disease that curls and thickens the leaves and twists the stem. There is no curative spray, and plants infected early give few, small, deformed pods.
symptoms: Leaves curl upward or downward and become thick and leathery
Small pin-head outgrowths (enations) on the veins under the leaf
Main stem and leaf stalks twist and bend
Stunted plants with few, small, deformed pods
Leaf curl virus.spread: Spread by whiteflies from infected okra and weed hosts, mostly in hot, dry weather; it is not carried by seed or soil.
Leaf curl virus.action: Pull out and destroy curled plants at once and spray thiamethoxam 25 WG 0.3 g/L to check whiteflies.

treatment.name: Roguing and resistant hybrids
treatment.notes: No spray cures the virus; remove infected plants early and grow a variety or hybrid released as resistant to leaf curl and yellow vein mosaic.

treatment.name: Thiamethoxam 25 WG
treatment.notes: Vector control only; pick pods before spraying and observe the label waiting period; spray in the evening, never on open flowers (toxic to bees).

treatment.name: Neem oil 1500 ppm
treatment.notes: Use between insecticide sprays and install yellow sticky traps for whitefly.

Phyllosticta leaf spot.name: Phyllosticta Leaf Spot
Phyllosticta leaf spot.description: A minor fungal leaf spot of okra seen in warm, wet weather. The spot centres dry and fall out, and badly spotted leaves dry and drop.
symptoms: Round to irregular ash-grey spots with a dark brown margin
Tiny black dots in the centre of the spots
Spot centres fall out leaving shot-holes
Badly spotted leaves dry and drop
Phyllosticta leaf spot.spread: Survives on infected crop debris and spreads by rain splash in warm, wet weather.
Phyllosticta leaf spot.action: Spray mancozeb 75 WP 2.5 g/L or copper oxychloride 50 WP 3 g/L at the first spots and repeat after 10-15 days if rain continues.

treatment.name: Mancozeb 75 WP
treatment.notes: Pick marketable pods before spraying and observe the label waiting period.

healthy.name: Healthy
healthy.description: The leaf shows no sign of disease, pest or nutrient problem. Keep up regular field scouting and balanced nutrition.
symptoms: Uniform green lobed leaves with green veins
No spots, mould, curling or yellow veins
Normal leaf size and steady new growth
healthy.action: Continue weekly scouting and watch for whiteflies and yellow veins on young leaves.
